before.name: Seated Floor Hamstring Stretch
instructions: Sit on a mat with your right leg extended in front of you and your left leg bent with your foot against your right inner thigh.
Lean forward from your hips and reach for your ankle until you feel a stretch in your hamstring. Hold for 15 seconds, then repeat for your other side.

before.name: Triceps Stretch

before.name: Shoulder Stretch

before.name: Side Neck Stretch

before.name: Calf Stretch Hands Against Wall

before.name: One-Arm Kettlebell Snatch
instructions: Place a kettlebell between your feet. Bend your knees and push your butt back to get in the proper starting position.
Look straight ahead and swing the kettlebell back between your legs.

Immediately reverse the direction and drive through with your hips and knees, accelerating the kettlebell upward. As the kettlebell rises to your shoulder rotate your hand and punch straight up, using momentum to receive the weight locked out overhead.

before.name: One-Arm Kettlebell Clean
instructions: Place a kettlebell between your feet. As you bend down to grab the kettlebell, push your butt back and keep your eyes looking forward.
Clean the kettlebell to your shoulders by extending through the legs and hips as you raise the kettlebell towards your shoulder. The wrist should rotate as you do so.
Return the weight to the starting position.

before.name: Kettlebell Sumo High Pull
instructions: Place a kettlebell on the ground between your feet. Position your feet in a wide stance, and grasp the kettlebell with two hands. Set your hips back as far as possible, with your knees bent. Keep your chest and head up. This will be your starting position.
Begin by extending the hips and knees, simultaneously pulling the kettlebell to your shoulders, raising your elbows as you do so. Reverse the motion to return to the starting position.

before.name: Single-leg BOSU balance
instructions: Single-Leg BOSU Balance Exercise

The exercise for balancing on a BOSU ball while standing on one leg is known as the single-leg BOSU balance exercise. This exercise is effective for enhancing balance, coordination, and core stability.
Benefits of the Single-Leg BOSU Balance Exercise
Improves Balance: Standing on one leg challenges your stability.
Enhances Coordination: Engaging different muscle groups helps improve overall coordination.
Strengthens Core: The exercise activates core muscles, promoting better posture and stability.
How to Perform the Single-Leg BOSU Balance Exercise
Positioning: Stand on the dome side of the BOSU ball with one leg.
Balance: Keep your opposite leg lifted and your core engaged.
Duration: Aim to hold the position for 10-20 seconds, gradually increasing the time as you improve.
Progression Tips
Add Movement: Try reaching for objects around you while maintaining balance.
Close Your Eyes: This increases the challenge by removing visual stability cues.
Use a Ball: Catch or toss a ball while balancing to further engage your core and coordination.
This exercise is a great way to build foundational balance skills before progressing to more complex movements.

before.name: Trap Bar Deadlift
instructions: For this exercise load a trap bar, also known as a hex bar, to an appropriate weight resting on the ground. Stand in the center of the apparatus and grasp both handles.
Lower your hips, look forward with your head and keep your chest up.
Begin the movement by driving through the heels and extend your hips and knees. Avoid rounding your back at all times.
At the completion of the movement, lower the weight back to the ground under control.

before.name: Butterfly
instructions: Sit on the machine with your back flat on the pad.
Take hold of the handles. Tip: Your upper arms should be positioned parallel to the floor; adjust the machine accordingly. This will be your starting position.
Push the handles together slowly as you squeeze your chest in the middle. Breathe out during this part of the motion and hold the contraction for a second.
Return back to the starting position slowly as you inhale until your chest muscles are fully stretched.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

before.name: Two-Arm Dumbbell Preacher Curl
instructions: Grab a dumbbell with each arm and place the upper arms on top of the preacher bench or the incline bench. The dumbbell should be held at shoulder length. This will be your starting position.
As you breathe in, slowly lower the dumbbells until your upper arm is extended and the biceps is fully stretched.
As you exhale, use the biceps to curl the weights up until your biceps is fully contracted and the dumbbells are at shoulder height.
Squeeze the biceps hard for a second at the contracted position and repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

before.name: Standing Cable Chest Press
instructions: Position dual pulleys to chest height and select an appropriate weight. Stand a foot or two in front of the cables, holding one in each hand. You can stagger your stance for better stability.
Position the upper arm at a 90 degree angle with the shoulder blades together. This will be your starting position.
Keeping the rest of the body stationary, extend through the elbows to press the handles forward, drawing them together in front of you.
Pause at the top of the motion, and return to the starting position.

before.name: Standing Toe Touches
instructions: Stand with some space in front and behind you.
Bend at the waist, keeping your legs straight, until you can relax and let your upper body hang down in front of you. Let your arms and hands hang down naturally. Hold for 10 to 20 seconds.

openGym.usage: Names and source IDs used for candidate lookup only. Numeric source ID matches are candidates, not verified equivalents. No OpenGym artwork, animations, generated derivatives or new AGPL descriptions copied.

muscleWiki.usage: Original branded MP4 footage and stills extracted from that footage for this personal/non-profit app; independent publisher terms retained.

workoutGuide.rejected: Hamstring stretch artwork elevates a leg on a rail and does not match bilateral toe-touch instructions. Standing quadriceps artwork matches, but original branded footage was available and used. No Workout Guide media imported in this continuation.

wger.usage: Candidate images without a supplied creator attribution or with an AI flag were not imported. Four existing attributed Goulart video sources were reviewed and converted under CC BY-SA 4.0.

duplicateDecisions.reason: Both specify sitting on floor with one leg straight and the other foot toward the inner thigh.
Both use self-assisted overhead elbow flexion with the other hand guiding the elbow.
Both hold a straight arm across the chest for a shoulder stretch.
Both use relaxed shoulders, a side head tilt and gentle hand assistance.
Both use a staggered stance, rear knee straight and rear heel grounded while hands support on wall.
Both swing one kettlebell into overhead lockout; not a two-bell snatch.
Both clean one bell to the shoulder rack with wrist rotation; not clean-and-press.
Both use a wide stance, two-hand single-bell grip and explosive hip drive into a high-elbow pull.
Both stand on one leg on the dome side of a BOSU; existing guidance includes optional ball tosses.
Archived definition describes the squat/deadlift combination performed inside a hex bar; no distinct pause, height or load setup is specified.
Both sit against the back pad and bring machine handles together for a pec fly, not a reverse fly.
Both curl two supinated dumbbells while upper arms rest on a preacher pad; existing hammer-grip curl remains distinct.
Despite its bench-press title, archived instructions explicitly stand facing away from chest-height dual cables.
Both describe a bilateral standing forward hinge reaching toward toes; supine strap stretches are distinct.
The archived standing option describes the same straight-leg forward hinge and hold; not a supine strap stretch.
Both kneel with elbows on a bench, palms together, elbows bent and chest lowered between the arms.
